entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo are taken at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do before arrival). Carry your passport when crossing borders inside Schengen.

tourism.detail: Australians are generally visa-exempt for short visits under Schengen rules.
tourism.next: Use SEM and the Swiss mission to check the current border position.

meetings.detail: Meetings, negotiations and congress attendance can fit a short visit; Swiss work law is separate from admission.
meetings.next: Carry the invitation and keep activity to meetings unless the host confirms work formalities.

conference.detail: Attendance and exhibition are not automatically permission to speak, train, install or perform.
conference.next: Ask the organiser and canton to classify any programme role.

unpaid-speaking.detail: Swiss notification and permit rules can distinguish short assignments, foreign employers and local work. Unpaid does not settle the question.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the host check SEM/cantonal rules for the exact role and days.

paid-speaking.detail: Paid speaking, consulting and teaching may need a notification procedure or permit, depending on duration, employer and nationality/sector.
paid-speaking.next: Let the Swiss engager lead the cantonal check before dates are public.

book-launch.route: Business visit for rights; cultural/work classification for launch
book-launch.detail: A publisher meeting may be a business visit; readings, signings, workshops and local sales need the host to classify delivery and tax.
book-launch.next: List royalties, fees, expenses, tickets and merchandise separately.

ai-teaching.detail: Academic exchange can use a host convention, but contracted training is local professional activity.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the university or company to identify the permit/notification path.

remote-work.detail: Switzerland has residence and work permits but no general remote-worker category. Tax residence and Swiss client activity remain distinct.
remote-work.next: Confirm canton, duration and employer/client location before relying on visitor entry.

entrepreneur.detail: A founder or independent professional needs cantonal economic-interest and residence approval; this is not an instant visitor conversion.
entrepreneur.next: Choose the canton and prepare the business, funding and economic-interest case.

trade.route: Short business visit; Swiss fulfilment needs work permission
trade.detail: Negotiation and sourcing can be visitor activity; installation, sales and delivery in Switzerland may not be.
trade.next: Map the Swiss customer, invoice and on-site work.

artist.detail: Performing, filming, exhibiting or touring is fact-dependent and can involve employer/organiser and cantonal permissions.
artist.next: Have the promoter specify venue, contract, fee, crew and dates.

mixed-mission.detail: Switzerland is an easy first arrival but not a blank cheque for local delivery.
mixed-mission.next: Send the schedule to the host canton as one precise activity brief.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of Switzerland, Forrest about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of Switzerland, Forrest if the host pays you.

volunteering.detail: Volunteering isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.
volunteering.next: Ask the Embassy of Switzerland, Forrest.

sources.title: Frequently asked questions on the Schengen visa-free regime
sources.supports: visa-free stays cover business meetings, journalistic or media purposes, short-term study or training; paid activity is excluded and needs national permission

consular.mission: Australian Embassy, Bern; Australian Consulate-General, Geneva
consular.notes: Consular assistance is available from the Australian Embassy in Bern and the Consulate-General in Geneva. The Embassy only provides routine passport services by appointment and as scheduled on the website. The Consulate-General in Geneva provides routine passport and notarial services by appointment and emergency passport services.
